origin.description: strsplit() that keeps the ANSI style of each piece.

arguments.name: split
arguments.text: One regular expression, or a literal when fixed is TRUE. An empty split breaks the string into characters.
Passed to gregexpr, including fixed and perl.

origin.details: The split is searched in the text with styles removed. Empty pieces at the ends are dropped, and an empty split also drops the empty first match. Each remaining span is taken with col_substring, so the pieces stay colored.
origin.value: A list of character vectors, one per input string.
origin.example:
s <- red("I am red---") %+% green("and I am green-") %+% underline("I underlined")
cat(col_strsplit(s, "[-]+")[[1]], sep="\n")

translation.description: strsplit() that keeps the ANSI style of each piece.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings.

arguments.name: split
arguments.text: One pattern. An empty string splits into characters.

arguments.name: fixed
arguments.text: When True, split is a literal, not a regular expression.

translation.details: The search uses Python's regular expressions. The empty-split and end-trimming rules follow crayon. The result is always a list of lists, one list of pieces per input string.
translation.value: A list of lists of strings.
translation.example:
text = concat(concat(red("I am red---"), green("and I am green-")), underline("I underlined"))
print("\n".join(col_strsplit(text, "[-]+")[0]))
